title: Maximum Employees to Be Invited to a Meeting
summary: A company plans a meeting with a circular table that can seat any number of employees.
statement: A company plans a meeting with a circular table that can seat any number of employees. Each employee, numbered from 0 to n-1, has a favorite person they must sit next to at the table to attend. Given an array favorite where favorite[i] is the favorite person of the i-th employee, determine the maximum number of employees that can be invited to the meeting.
constraints: Each employee favors exactly one different employee and must sit beside that person at a circular table.
Invite a subset and arrange it around one circle.
Return the maximum possible invited count.
hints: After pruning noncycle nodes, only directed cycles remain; incoming chains can attach only to the ends of mutual pairs.
Topologically remove trees while recording longest depth into each node.
Take the maximum of the longest cycle and the sum of both chain depths for every two-cycle.
Longer cycles fill both neighbor seats and cannot accept chains, while separate mutual-pair components and their best chains can be concatenated around one table.
editorial: Longer cycles fill both neighbor seats and cannot accept chains, while separate mutual-pair components and their best chains can be concatenated around one table.

tests.explanation: Employees one and two form a mutual pair, and one incoming employee can sit on its outer side, totaling three.
The three employees form a cycle and can all sit together.
